article.title: SaxonC API
article.p: This section describes the SaxonC API. The APIs support the XSLT 3.0, XQuery 3.1, XPath 3.1 and Schema Validation 1.0/1.1 specifications. SaxonC can be used in C/C++, PHP and Python, and links to the APIs in each of these languages are provided below.
For C++, PHP and Python, the SaxonC API provides six main classes:

td.p: A SaxonProcessor acts as a factory for generating XSLT, XQuery, XPath and Schema compilers. This class creates the GraalVM Native Image run time data structure for a thread in a static struct object which is shared across all SaxonProcessor objects created. For C++ programs the static method SaxonProcessor::release() needs to be called at the end of a program to clean up the GraalVM threads. In the SaxonC Python and PHP extensions this release method is called internally.

An Xslt30Processor represents a factory to compile, load and execute stylesheets. The name of the class refers to the fact that this XSLT processor supports options for invoking a stylesheet corresponding to the new facilities defined in the XSLT 3.0 specification. But the processor can of course also process XSLT 2.0 and XSLT 1.0 stylesheets.
An XsltExecutable represents the compiled form of a stylesheet. An XsltExecutable is created using one of the compile methods on the Xslt30Processor class.
An XQueryProcessor represents a factory to compile, load and execute queries.
An XPathProcessor represents a factory to compile, load and execute XPath expressions.
A SchemaValidator represents a factory for validating instance documents against a schema.

article.p: For C, the SaxonC API is provided in the three header files: SaxonCGlue.h, SaxonCProcessor.h, SaxonCXPath.h.
For further information about these APIs see the following sections:

The SaxonC APIs provide a custom-designed interface for all XML processing. The APIs are useful when you want to write your own applications in C/C++, Python or PHP to invoke XSLT transforms, XQuery, XPath evaluation, or XML Schema validation with Saxon. For more information on how to get started using these APIs, see the relevant sections in the main Saxon documentation:

li.a: XSLT transformations from a C/C++, Python or PHP application
XQuery from a C/C++, Python or PHP application
Evaluating XPath expressions from a C/C++, Python or PHP application
Validation from C/C++, Python or PHP

section.title: SaxonC C++ API
section.p: SaxonC 12 is built from the SaxonJ 12 Java product by compiling using GraalVM Native Image. This generates platform specific machine code, which is interfaced with C/C++ using the Native Image C API.
The SaxonC C/C++ API documentation contains full details of the API. See below for direct links to the main classes.

section.title: SaxonC PHP API
section.p: The following classes are available in the PHP API:

section.title: Saxon\SaxonProcessor
section.p: The SaxonProcessor class acts as a factory for generating XSLT, XQuery, XPath and Schema processors. It is also used to create XDM objects from primitive types.

td.div: Default Constructor. Create an unlicensed Saxon Processor.

Constructor. Indicates whether the Processor requires features of Saxon that need a license file. If false, the method will create a Configuration appropriate for Saxon-HE (Home edition). If true, the method will create a Configuration appropriate to the version of the software that is running, i.e. Saxon-PE or Saxon-EE.

Constructor. Indicates whether the Processor requires features of Saxon that need a license file. The $cwd argument is used to manually set the current working directory used for executions of source files.
Convert clark name string to EQName notation.
Convert EQName string to clark name notation.
Create an XDM atomic value from any of the main primitive types (i.e. bool, int, float, double, string).
Create an XDM QName from a string representing the QName in Clark notation.
Make an XdmArray whose argument is a PHP array_map with keys of type integer and values of type XdmValue (or a subclass of XdmValue).
Make an XdmMap whose argument is a PHP array_map with key and value pair as (string, XdmValue).

Create an XdmNode object. The $value is a lexical representation of the XML document. The optional $encoding argument can be used to specify the encoding used to decode the string; if not specified then the platform default encoding is used. The optional $validator argument can be used to supply a SchemaValidator to validate the document (the default is NULL).

Create an XdmNode object by parsing an XML document, as specified by the $fileName argument. The file name can be relative or absolute. If relative the cwd is used to resolve the file. The optional $validator argument can be used to supply a SchemaValidator to validate the document (the default is NULL).
Create an XdmNode object by parsing an XML document, as available by URI.
Set the current working directory used to resolve file names against.
Set a catalog to be used in Saxon.
Set a configuration property specific to the processor in use. Properties specified here are common across all the processors. See Configuration features for more details.
Create an DocumentBuilder Create a DocumentBuilder. A DocumentBuilder is used to load source XML documents.

Create an Xslt30Processor in the PHP environment specifically designed for XSLT 3.0 processing. An Xslt30Processor is used to compile and execute XSLT 3.0 stylesheets, but can also be used for XSLT 2.0 or 1.0 stylesheets.
Create an XQueryProcessor in the PHP environment. An XQueryProcessor is used to compile and execute XQuery queries.
Create an XPathProcessor in the PHP environment. An XPathProcessor is used to compile and execute XPath expressions.

Create a SchemaValidator in the PHP environment. A SchemaValidator provides capabilities to load and cache XML schema definitions. You can also validate source documents with registered XML schema definitions.
Report the Saxon version.
Enables the ability to use PHP functions as XSLT functions. Accepts as parameter the full path of the SaxonC PHP Extension library. This is needed to do the callbacks.

section.title: Saxon\Xslt30Processor
section.p: An Xslt30Processor represents a factory to compile, load and execute stylesheets. It is possible to cache the context and the stylesheet in the Xslt30Processor.

td.div: Get the stylesheet associated via the xml-stylesheet processing instruction (see http://www.w3.org/TR/xml-stylesheet/) in the document specified in the $xmlFileName argument, and that match the given criteria. If there are several suitable xml-stylesheet processing instructions, then the returned source will identify a synthesized stylesheet module that imports all the referenced stylesheet modules.
Compile a stylesheet supplied as a file as specified by the $fileName argument.
Compile a stylesheet received as a string. The optional $encoding argument can be used to specify the encoding used to decode the string; if not specified then the platform default encoding is used.
Compile a stylesheet received as an XdmNode.
Compile a stylesheet supplied as a file as specified by the $fileName argument, and save as an exported file (SEF).
Compile a stylesheet received as a string and save as an exported file (SEF).
Compile a stylesheet received as an XdmNode and save as an exported file (SEF).

Calling this method makes the supplied package available for reference in the xsl:use-package declarations of subsequent compilations performed using this Saxon\Xslt30Processor. The package to be imported should be supplied as an SEF; the file name of this SEF is specified by the $packageFileName argument. If relative, the file name is resolved against the cwd, which is set using setcwd().

Set the current working directory (cwd). This method also applies to the static base URI for XSLT stylesheets when supplied as lexical string. The cwd is used to set the base URI is part of the static context, and is used to resolve any relative URIs appearing within XSLT.
Perform a one shot transformation, saving the results to the file specified in the $outputFileName argument.

Perform a one shot transformation. The $sourceFileName argument is the name of the source file. The $stylesheetFileName argument is the name of the stylesheet file. The result is returned as an XdmValue.

Perform a one shot transformation. The $sourceFileName argument is the name of the source file. The $stylesheetFileName argument is the name of the stylesheet file. The result is returned as a string.
Perform a one shot transformation. The global context item may be supplied in the $context argument, but this is optional - the method will also execute without any arguments.
Set the parameters required for the XSLT stylesheet.
Say whether just-in-time compilation of template rules should be used.
Set the target edition under which the stylesheet will be executed. The $edition argument is the Saxon edition for the run-time environment: one of "EE", "PE", "HE", or "JS", "JS2", or "JS3".

Set the XSLT (and XPath) language level to be supported by the processor. Set the value to "4.0" to enable support for experimental features defined in the XSLT 4.0 proposal (which is likely to change before it stabilizes).The values "3.0" and "4.0" are recognized.

Request fast compilation. This will generally be achieved at the expense of run-time performance and quality of diagnostics. Fast compilation is a good trade-off if (a) the stylesheet is known to be correct, and (b) once compiled, it is only executed once against a document of modest size.

Indicate whether any package produced by this compiler can be deployed to a different location, with a different base URI. If true then static-base-uri() represents the deployed location of the package, rather than its compile time location.
Clear parameter values set.
Clear any exceptions thrown.
Get the error code if there is an error.
Get the error message if there is an error.
Get the number of errors during execution or evaluation of a stylesheet.

section.title: Saxon\XsltExecutable
section.p: An XsltExecutable represents the compiled form of a stylesheet. An XsltExecutable is created by using one of the compile methods on the Xslt30Processor class.

td.div: Invoke the most recently compiled stylesheet by applying templates to a supplied input sequence (the initial match selection), saving the results to the file specified in the $outputfileName argument.
Invoke a stylesheet by applying templates to a supplied input sequence (the initial match selection). The result is returned as a serialized string.
Invoke a stylesheet by applying templates to a supplied input sequence (the initial match selection). The result is returned as an XdmValue object.

Call a public user-defined function in the stylesheet. Here we wrap the result in an XML document, and send this document to a specified file. The function name is supplied as a string, and the values of the arguments to be supplied to the function are supplied as an array of XdmValue objects. These will be converted if necessary to the type as defined in the function signature, using the function conversion rules.

Call a public user-defined function in the stylesheet. Here we wrap the result in an XML document, and serialize this document to a string value. The function name is supplied as a string, and the values of the arguments to be supplied to the function are supplied as an array of XdmValue objects. These will be converted if necessary to the type as defined in the function signature, using the function conversion rules.

Call a public user-defined function in the stylesheet. Here we wrap the result in an XML document, and return the document as an XdmValue. The function name is supplied as a string, and the values of the arguments to be supplied to the function are supplied as an array of XdmValue objects. These will be converted if necessary to the type as defined in the function signature, using the function conversion rules.
Create a clone of this Saxon\XsltExecutable object.

Invoke a transformation by calling a named template, saving the results to the file specified in the $outputFileName argument. If the $templateName argument is null then the xsl:initial-template is used. Parameters supplied using setInitialTemplateParameters() are made available to the called template.

Invoke a transformation by calling a named template, and return the result as a string. If the $templateName argument is null then the xsl:initial-template is used. Parameters supplied using setInitialTemplateParameters() are made available to the called template.

Invoke a transformation by calling a named template, and return the result as an XdmValue. If the $templateName argument is null then the xsl:initial-template is used. Parameters supplied using setInitialTemplateParameters() are made available to the called template.

Produce a representation of the compiled stylesheet. The representation of the compiled stylesheet is in an XML form, suitable for distribution and reloading. If the configuration under which the export takes place is suitably licensed, then license information will be included in the export file allowing execution of the stylesheet without any additional license. The detailed form of the output representation is not documented. The argument $fileName is the destination for the XML document containing the diagnostic representation of the compiled stylesheet. The stream will be closed when writing has finished.
Perform a one shot transformation, saving the results to the file specified in the $outputFileName argument.
Perform a one shot transformation. The result is returned as an XdmValue.
Perform a one shot transformation. The result is returned as a string.

Perform a one shot transformation, saving the results to the file as previously set (e.g. using setOutputFile()). The global context item may be supplied in the $context argument, but this is optional - the method will also execute without any arguments.

Perform a one shot transformation. The result is returned as a serialized string. The global context item may be supplied in the $context argument, but this is optional - the method will also execute without any arguments.

Perform a one shot transformation. The result is returned as an XdmValue object. If there are failures then a null is returned. The global context item may be supplied in the $context argument, but this is optional - the method will also execute without any arguments.
Set the current working directory used to resolve file names against.

This method gives users the option to switch on or off the xsl:message feature. The boolean argument $show is used to indicate if xsl:message should be outputted. Default is on. It is also possible to send the xsl:message outputs to a file specified by argument $filename.

Get the messages written using the xsl:message instruction. Returns null if the user has not enabled capturing of xsl:message outputs via setSaveXslMessage(). Returns the sequence of xsl:messages as an XdmValue.

Enable the capture of the result-document output into an XdmMap. If this option is enabled, then any document created using xsl:result-document is saved (as an XdmNode) in a XdmMap object where it is accessible using the URI as a key. After the execution of the transformation a call on the getResultDocuments() method is required to get access to the result-documents in the map. Supplying true for the $flag parameter causes secondary result documents from the transformation to be saved in a map; false disables this option.

Return the result-documents resulting from the execution of the stylesheet. Null is returned if the user has not enabled this feature via the method setCaptureResultDocuments(). Returns a XdmMap indexed by the absolute URI of the result document, and the corresponding value is an XdmNode containing the result document (as an in-memory tree, without serialization).

Set the base output URI. The $baseOutputURI argument is supplied as a string value. The base output URI is used for resolving relative URIs in the href attribute of the xsl:result-document instruction; it is accessible to XSLT stylesheet code using the XPath current-output-uri() function.

Set the initial mode for the transformation. The $modeName argument is supplied as the EQName of the initial mode. Two special values are recognized, in the reserved XSLT namespace: xsl:unnamed to indicate the mode with no name, and xsl:default to indicate the mode defined in the stylesheet header as the default mode. The value null also indicates the default mode (which defaults to the unnamed mode, but can be set differently in an XSLT 3.0 stylesheet).

Set parameters to be passed to the initial template. These are used whether the transformation is invoked by applying templates to an initial context item, or by invoking a named template. The parameters in question are the xsl:param elements appearing as children of the xsl:template element. The $tunnel argument should be set to true if these values are to be used for setting tunnel parameters.
Set the initial value to which templates are to be applied (equivalent to the 'select' attribute of xsl:apply-templates).

Set the initial value to which templates are to be applied (equivalent to the 'select' attribute of xsl:apply-templates). This initial match selection is supplied as a file as specified by the $fileName argument.
Supply the context item to be used when evaluating global variables and parameters.
Supply the context item to be used when evaluating global variables and parameters, as a file as specified by the $fileName argument.
Set the output file to which the transformation result will be sent.
Set the parameters required for the XSLT stylesheet.
Set properties for the XSLT processor.
Say whether just-in-time compilation of template rules should be used.
Set true if the result of a transformation should be returned as a raw XdmValue result, rather than as a result tree (an XdmNode object with a Document node as its root).
Clear parameter values set.
Clear property values set.
Clear any exceptions thrown.
Get the error code if there is an error.
Get the error message if there is an error.
Get the number of errors during execution or evaluation of a stylesheet.

section.title: Saxon\XQueryProcessor
section.p: An XQueryProcessor represents a factory to compile, load and execute queries.

td.div: Compile and evaluate the query. Result returned as an XdmValue object. If there are failures then a null is returned.
Compile and evaluate the query. Result returned as a string. If there are failures then a null is returned.
Compile and evaluate the query. Result saved to the file specified in the $outputFileName argument.

Set the XQuery (and XPath) language level to be supported by the processor. Set the value to "4.0" to enable support for experimental features defined in the XQuery 4.0 proposal (which is likely to change before it stabilizes). Currently, the values "3.1" and "4.0" are recognized.

Say whether the query should be compiled and evaluated to use streaming. This affects subsequent calls on the compile() methods. This option requires Saxon-EE. If true, the compiler will attempt to compile a query to be capable of executing in streaming mode. If the query cannot be streamed, a compile-time exception is reported. In streaming mode, the source document is supplied as a stream, and no tree is built in memory. The default is false.
Ask whether the streaming option has been set, that is, whether subsequent calls on compile() will compile queries to be capable of executing in streaming mode.
Query supplied as a string.
Query supplied as a file as specified by the $fileName argument.
Set the initial context item for the query, supplied as a file as specified by the $fileName argument.
Set the initial context item for the query. Any one of the following objects is accepted: XdmItem, XdmNode and XdmAtomicValue.
Set the static base URI for a query expression compiled using this XQuery Processor. The base URI is part of the static context, and is used to resolve any relative URIs appearing within a query.
Declare a namespace binding as part of the static context for XPath expressions compiled using this XQuery processor.
Set the parameters required for the query.
Set properties for the XQuery processor.
Clear parameter values set.
Clear property values set.
Clear any exceptions thrown.
Get the error code if there is an error.
Get the error message if there is an error.
Get the number of errors during execution or evaluation of a query.

section.title: Saxon\XPathProcessor
section.p: An XPathProcessor represents a factory to compile, load and execute XPath expressions.

td.div: Set the context item from an XdmItem.
Set the context item, supplied as a file as specified by the $fileName argument.
Evaluate the supplied XPath expression, returning the effective boolean value of the result.
Compile and evaluate an XPath expression, supplied as a character string, returning the result as an XdmValue.

Compile and evaluate an XPath expression whose result is expected to be a single item, with a given context item. The expression is supplied as a character string, and the result returned as an XdmItem. Returns null if the expression returns an empty sequence. If the expression returns a sequence of more than one item, any items after the first are ignored.
Declare a namespace binding as part of the static context for XPath expressions compiled using this XPath processor.

div.p: Declare a variable as part of the static context for XPath expressions compiled using this XPathCompiler.

It is an error for the XPath expression to refer to a variable unless it has been declared. This method declares the existence of the variable, but it does not bind any value to the variable; that is done later, when the XPath expression is evaluated. The variable is allowed to have any type (that is, the required type is item()*).
The name of the variable must be supplied as a string representing the QName in Clark notation.

td.div: Say whether XPath 1.0 backwards compatibility mode is to be used. In backwards compatibility mode, more implicit type conversions are allowed in XPath expressions, for example it is possible to compare a number with a string. The default is false (backwards compatibility mode is off).

Say whether the compiler should maintain a cache of compiled expressions. If the argument $caching is set to true, caching of compiled expressions is enabled. If set to false, any existing cache is cleared, and future compiled expressions will not be cached until caching is re-enabled. The cache is also cleared (but without disabling future caching) if any method is called that changes the static context for compiling expressions, for example declareVariable() or declareNamespace().

div.p: Import a schema namespace. Here we add the element and attribute declarations and type definitions contained in a given namespace to the static context for the XPath expression.

This method will not cause the schema to be loaded. This method will not fail if the schema has not been loaded (but in that case the set of declarations and definitions made available to the XPath expression is empty). The schema document for the specified namespace may be loaded before or after this method is called.
This method does not bind a prefix to the namespace. That must be done separately, using the declareNamespace() method.
The argument $uri is the schema namespace to be imported. To import declarations in a no-namespace schema, supply a zero-length string.
Set the policy for matching unprefixed element names in XPath expressions.

DEFAULT_NAMESPACE = 0 - The standard W3C policy, whereby element names are implicitly qualified by the default namespace for elements and types, as defined in the XPath static context. This is set with the number value 0.

DEFAULT_NAMESPACE_OR_NONE = 2 - this policy is provided primarily for use with HTML, where it can be unpredictable whether HTML elements are in the XHTML namespace or in no namespace. It is also useful with other vocabularies where instances are sometimes in a namespace and sometimes not. The policy approximates to the special rules defined in the HTML5 specification. This is set with the number value 2.

td.div: Set the static base URI for XPath expressions compiled using this XPath processor. The base URI is part of the static context, and is used to resolve any relative URIs appearing within an XPath expression.
Set the parameters required for the XPath expression.
Set properties for the XPath processor.
Clear parameter values set.
Clear property values set.
Clear any exceptions thrown.
Get the error code if there is an error.
Get the error message if there is an error.
Get the number of errors during execution or evaluation of an XPath expression.

section.title: Saxon\SchemaValidator
section.p: A SchemaValidator represents a factory for validating instance documents against a schema.

td.div: Set the instance document to be validated, supplied as an XdmNode.
Set the file to which a validated document will be saved if validation is successful. The supplied file name is resolved and accessed.

The validation mode may be either strict or lax. The default is strict; this method may be called to indicate that lax validation is required. With strict validation, validation fails if no element declaration can be located for the outermost element. With lax validation, the absence of an element declaration results in the content being considered valid. If the argument $lax is true then validation is to be lax, if false then validation is strict.
Register a schema document supplied as an XdmNode, as specified by the $node argument.

Register a schema file supplied as a file name as specified by the $fileName argument. The document may be either a schema document in source XSD format, or a compiled schema in Saxon-defined SCM format (as produced using the exportSchema() method).
Register a schema supplied as a string.

Export a precompiled Schema Component Model containing all the components (except built-in components) that have been loaded by using the register methods. The $filename argument is the file name where the exported schema will be stored.
Validate an instance document, which has already been supplied through other accessor methods.
Validate an instance document supplied as a file as specified by the $fileName argument. $fileName can be null.
Validate an instance document, which has already been supplied through other accessor methods, with the validated document returned to the calling program.
Validate an instance document supplied as a file (as specified by the $fileName argument), with the validated document returned to the calling program. $fileName can be null.

Get the validation report produced after validating the source document. The reporting feature is switched on by setting the 'report' property on the SchemaValidator: e.g. validator.setProperty('report', 'true'). Returns the report as an XdmNode.
Set the parameters required for the schema.
Set properties for this SchemaValidator.
Clear parameter values set.
Clear property values set.
Clear any exceptions thrown.
Get the error code if there is an error.
Get the error message if there is an error.
Get the number of errors during execution of the validation.

section.title: Saxon\DocumentBuilder
section.p: A DocumentBuilder holds properties controlling how a Saxon document tree should be built, and provides methods to invoke the tree construction.
This class has no public constructor. To construct a DocumentBuilder, use the factory method newDocumentBuilder() of SaxonProcessor.

td.div: If the argument $option is true this enables line and column numbering for documents constructed using this DocumentBuilder. This has the effect that the line and column number in the original source document is maintained in the constructed tree, for each element node (and only for elements). The line and column number in question are generally the position at which the closing ">" of the element start tag appears. By default, line and column numbers are not maintained. Errors relating to document parsing and validation will generally contain line numbers whether or not this option is set, because such errors are detected during document construction. Line numbering is not available for all kinds of source: for example, it is not available when loading from an existing DOM Document.
Ask whether line and column numbering is enabled for documents loaded using this DocumentBuilder. By default, line and column numbering is disabled.

Set the SchemaValidator to be used. This determines whether schema validation is applied to an input document and whether type annotations in a supplied document are retained. If no SchemaValidator is supplied, then schema validation does not take place. This option requires the schema-aware version of the Saxon product (Saxon-EE). Since a SchemaValidator is serially reusable but not thread-safe, using this method is not appropriate when the DocumentBuilder is shared between threads.
Get the SchemaValidator used to validate documents loaded using this DocumentBuilder.
Set whether DTD validation should be applied to documents loaded using this DocumentBuilder. By default, no DTD validation takes place.
Ask whether DTD validation is to be applied to documents loaded using this DocumentBuilder.

Set the base URI of a document loaded using this DocumentBuilder. This is used for resolving any relative URIs appearing within the document, for example in references to DTDs and external entities. This information is required when the document is loaded from a source that does not provide an intrinsic URI, notably when loading from a String. The value is ignored when loading from a source that does have an intrinsic base URI.
Get the base URI of documents loaded using this DocumentBuilder when no other URI is available.
Build a document from a supplied URI source.

Build a document from a lexical string representation, to create a tree representation of the document in memory. The optional $encoding argument can be used to specify the encoding used to decode the string; if not specified then the platform default encoding is used.
Build a document from a supplied XML file.
Checks for pending exceptions. Returns true when there is a pending exception; otherwise returns false.
Clear any exception thrown.
Get the error message if there is an error.
Get the error code if there is an error.

section.title: Saxon\XdmValue
section.p: An XdmValue represents a value in the XDM data model. A value is a sequence of zero or more items, each item being an atomic value, a node, or a function item.

td.div: Get the first item in the sequence.
Get the n'th item in the sequence, counting from zero.
Get the number of items in the sequence.
Add an item to the end of the sequence.

section.title: Saxon\XdmItem
section.p: extends Saxon\XdmValue
The class XdmItem represents an item in a sequence, as defined by the XDM data model. An item is either an atomic value, a node, or a function item.

td.div: Get the string value of the item. For a node, this gets the string value of the node. For an atomic value, this has the same effect as casting the value to a string. In all cases the result is the same as applying the XPath string() function.
Determine whether or not the item is a node.
Determine whether or not the item is an atomic value.
If the item is an atomic value, then this XdmAtomicValue is returned; otherwise returns null.
If the item is a node, then this XdmNode is returned; otherwise returns null.

section.title: Saxon\XdmAtomicValue
section.p: extends Saxon\XdmItem

The class PyXdmAtomicValue represents an item in an XPath sequence that is an atomic value. The value may belong to any of the 19 primitive types defined in XML Schema, or to a type derived from these primitive types, or the XPath type xs:untypedAtomic.

td.div: Get the string value of the item. For an atomic value, this has the same effect as casting the value to a string. In all cases the result is the same as applying the XPath string() function.
Get the value converted to a boolean using the XPath casting rules.
Get the value converted to a double using the XPath casting rules. If the value is a string, the XSD 1.1 rules are used, which means that the string "+INF" is recognised.
Get the value converted to an integer using the XPath casting rules.
Determine whether or not the item is an atomic value. This method will return TRUE as the item is atomic.

section.title: Saxon\XdmNode
section.p: extends Saxon\XdmItem

This class represents a node in the XDM data model. An XdmNode is an XdmItem, and is therefore an XdmValue in its own right, and may also participate as one item within a sequence value. The XdmNode interface exposes basic properties of the node, such as its name, its string value, and its typed value.

td.div: Get the string value of the node.
Get the kind of node.
Get the name of the node, as an EQName.
Determine whether or not the item is an atomic value. This method will return FALSE as the item is not atomic.
Get the number of child nodes of this node.
Get the number of attribute nodes of this node.
Get the n'th child node of this node. If the child node selected does not exist then return null.

Get the array of nodes reachable from this node via a given axis. The $axis parameter identifies which axis is to be navigated. Axis options are as follows: ANCESTOR = 0, ANCESTOR_OR_SELF = 1, ATTRIBUTE = 2, CHILD = 3, DESCENDANT = 4, DESCENDANT_OR_SELF = 5, FOLLOWING = 6, FOLLOWING_SIBLING = 7, NAMESPACE = 8, PARENT = 9, PRECEDING = 10, PRECEDING_SIBLING = 11 and SELF = 12. Returns an XdmValue containing a sequence of XDM nodes on the specified axis, starting from this node as the context node. The nodes are returned in axis order, that is, in document order for a forwards axis and in reverse document order for a reverse axis.
Get the parent node of this node. If a parent node does not exist then return null.
Get the n'th attribute node of this node. If the attribute node selected does not exist then return null.
Get the value of the n'th attribute node of this node. If the attribute node selected does not exist then return null.

section.title: Saxon\XdmFunctionItem
section.p: extends Saxon\XdmItem
The class XdmFunctionItem represents a function item.

td.div: Get the name of the function in EQName notation, i.e. Q{uri}local. Returns null for an anonymous inline function item.
Get the arity of the function. The arity of the function, that is, the number of arguments in the function's signature.

Get a system function. This can be any function defined in XPath 3.1 functions and operators, including functions in the math, map, and array namespaces. It can also be a Saxon extension function, provided a licensed Processor is used. The first argument is used to supply the SaxonProcessor required to get the system function. The second argument is used to provide the name of the requested function, and the last argument its arity. Returns the requested function, or null if there is no such function. Note that some functions (those with particular context dependencies) may be unsuitable for dynamic calling.

Call the function. The first argument is used to supply the SaxonProcessor required for the calling of the function. The values of the arguments to be supplied to the function are supplied as an array of XdmValue objects. The "function conversion rules" will be applied to convert the arguments to the required type when necessary. Returns the result of calling the function as an XdmValue.

section.title: Saxon\XdmArray
section.p: extends Saxon\XdmFunctionItem

The class XdmArray represents an array in the XDM data model. An array is a list of zero or more members, each of which is an arbitrary XDM value. The array itself is an XDM item. An XdmArray is immutable.

td.div: Get the number of members in the array. (Note that the size() method returns 1, because an XDM array is an item.)
Get the n'th item in the array, counting from zero.

Create a new array in which one member is replaced with a new value. The argument $n is the position of the member that is to be replaced, counting the first member in the array as member zero. $value is the new member in the returned new array.
Append a new member to an array. The returned new array is one item longer than the original. Note: if the value is lazily evaluated, and evaluation fails then return null.
Concatenate another array. Returns a new array, containing the members of this array followed by the members of the array supplied in the $value argument.

section.title: Saxon\XdmMap
section.p: extends Saxon\XdmFunctionItem

The class XdmMap represents a map item in the XDM data model. A map is a list of zero or more entries, each of which is a pair comprising a key (which is an atomic value) and a value (which is an arbitrary value). The map itself is an XDM item. A XdmMap is immutable.

td.div: Get the number of entries in the map. (Note that the size() method returns 1, because an XDM map is an item.)
Returns the value to which the specified key is mapped, or null if this map contains no mapping for the key. The argument $key specifies the key of the entry, as an XdmAtomicValue.

Returns the value to which the specified string-valued key is mapped, or null if this map contains no mapping for the key. This is a convenience method to save the trouble of converting the String to an XdmAtomicValue.

Returns the value to which the specified integer-valued key is mapped or null if this map contains no mapping for the key. This is a convenience method to save the trouble of converting the integer to an XdmAtomicValue.

Create a new map containing an additional (key, value) pair. If there is an existing entry with the same key, it is removed. Returns a new map containing the additional entry. The original map is unchanged.

Create a new map in which the entry for a given key has been removed. If there is no entry with the specified key, the new map has the same content as the old (it may or may not be the same object). The argument $key specifies the key of the entry to be removed, as an XdmAtomicValue. Returns a new map without the specified entry. The original map is unchanged.
Returns true if this map contains no entries.
Returns true if this map contains an entry for the specified key.

section.title: SaxonC C API
section.p: SaxonC 12 is built from the SaxonJ 12 Java product by compiling using GraalVM Native Image. This generates platform specific machine code, which is interfaced with C/C++ using the Native Image C API.
The SaxonC C/C++ API documentation contains full details of the API to process XSLT, XQuery, and XPath.
The SaxonC C API is provided in the following header files:

ul.li: SaxonCProcessor.h - consists of functions to compile and execute XSLT 3.0 stylesheets and XQuery 3.1 queries.
SaxonCXPath.h - consists of functions to compile and evaluate XPath 3.1 expressions.
